title: Snowflake — advanced
subtitle: A six-branch lace snowflake with secondary branches and picot tips
excerpt: This advanced snowflake extends each of the six main branches with two secondary branches, giving the motif its characteristic feathered appearance. Picot tips at each branch end sharpen the silhouette. Five rounds in 4-ply cotton produce a 14 cm snowflake that blocks flat and crisp.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Needlework, Volume 7 (1892), snowflake lace chapter (Internet Archive). Victorian snowflake motifs appeared as Christmas decorations and as applique for net veiling.
heroPrompt: An advanced crochet snowflake in fine white 4-ply cotton on a pale linen background, photographed flat from above in soft daylight. Six main branches with two secondary branches each, picot tips at every branch end, 14 cm across.

crochet.gaugeText: Finished advanced snowflake measures 14 cm across in 4-ply cotton with a 2.5 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Snowflake — advanced
chartDefinition.caption: Six main branches with secondary branches. Each branch built from chain arches anchored at the centre ring.

glossaryTerms.definition: A chain-3 loop anchored back to itself at the tip of a branch or point. It sharpens the end of the branch and adds a decorative bead-like dot at the tip.

content.text: The advanced snowflake works the six main branches as chain-10 arches in round 1, then fills each branch with dc and adds secondary branches and
on round 2. Each main branch gets two secondary branches at one-third and two-third positions along its length.

Use 4-ply cotton and a 2.5 mm hook. Work at a relaxed, even tension — tight tension makes the chain arches short and stiff. Block the finished snowflake by wetting, pinning all 18 branch tips (6 main + 12 secondary) to the blocking mat, and leaving to dry for several hours.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 8 g of white or natural 4-ply cotton thread. A 2.5 mm hook. Blocking mat, 20 pins.

content.text: Magic ring. *Ch 10. Sl st back into ring.* Rep 6 times. Pull ring closed. (6 ch-10 branch arches.)

Work along each main branch as follows: 4 dc along the chain. *Ch 5. Sl st back to the 4th dc (secondary branch loop). Fill loop: 6 dc into ch-5 arch. Sl st to close secondary branch.* Work 2 dc more. Rep the secondary branch process (ch 5 arch and 6 dc fill). Work remaining 4 dc to the tip. Picot tip: ch 3, sl st back into the last dc. Continue dc back toward centre. Sl st to ring between branches. Rep for all 6 main branches. Fasten off.
Work the granny stripe panel for a different approach to joining motifs into a striped panel without additional seaming.
